subject: PolarisWorks partnership — solution gate & reference design checklist
messages:
From: Diane Nguyen <diane.nguyen@polarisworks.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
Cc: partnerships@polarisworks.com
Date: Wed, 22 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: PolarisWorks x Redwood — request for solution gate review

Hi Tessa,

Thanks again for the call last week. PolarisWorks is moving toward a joint reference integration for our managed deployment orchestration and we want Redwood to be the recommended inference endpoint. Before we start engineering work, our architecture and security teams asked for a short technical validation so we can sign off on the reference design.

Attached: polaris_integration_spec_v1.pdf (PDF) — high-level flow, KPIs; polaris-network-diagram.png (PNG).

Top asks from our side:
- Confirm feasibility of prefix caching and expected cost impact at 2k qps
- Identify gating criteria for a public reference (latency SLOs, failover behavior)
- Define a minimal smoke test plan we can run in the Polaris pre-prod environment

Can we schedule a 45-minute review with your architecture and partner teams early next week? Diane

Diane Nguyen
Head of Integrations | PolarisWorks
D: +1 415-555-0142
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Diane Nguyen <diane.nguyen@polarisworks.com>
Cc: sergio_alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 22 Mar 2028 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: PolarisWorks x Redwood — request for solution gate review

Hi Diane — great to hear. Happy to run the technical validation.

Proposed agenda for the 45-minute session:
1) Quick architecture read (5m) — confirm traffic patterns and hosting mode
2) Performance & cost model (10m) — expected token cost at 2k qps; KV/prefix caching impact
3) Resilience & failover (10m) — routing policies and fallback model variants
4) Gating criteria & smoke tests (15m) — pass/fail checklist we both sign off on
5) Next steps & owners (5m)

Sergio (partner eng) and Laura (solutions) are looped in to cover runbook and acceptance criteria.

Available windows (PST): Mon 2028-03-27 09:00–11:00 or Tue 2028-03-28 13:00–15:00. Which works for your team?

Also: can you confirm whether Polaris pre-prod will terminate TLS at the edge or pass-through to Redwood? That changes our recommended cert/KMS notes.

Thanks,

—
Tessa Morgan
Head of Partnerships | Redwood Inference

Attaching a short network ACL snapshot and our SOC pointer. We'll keep procurement in the loop but they won't need to attend the technical session.

Best,
Diane

Attachments: polaris-network-acls.txt (TXT)
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
To: sergio_alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 23 Mar 2028 09:07:00 -07:00
Subject: PolarisWorks validation — internal prep + gating checklist

Sergio/Laura — quick prep before Tuesday's call with Polaris. I captured the high-level asks from Diane and sketched a lightweight pass/fail checklist for the reference design. Please review and add items.

Draft gating criteria (we should keep it lean):
- Latency: 95th percentile <= 220ms for 512-token request at steady load (2k qps simulated across multiple clients)
- Availability: no more than 3 1-minute recovery incidents in a 24-hour window during smoke run
- Correctness: sample prompt set (see RWI-sample-assertions.xlsx) must have >= 98% parity vs baseline model outputs (semantic similarity > 0.9)
- Failover: automated fallback to smaller model variant within 500ms upon node loss
- Security: TLS pass-through validated; KMS key access verified for the test tenant

Suggested minimal smoke tests (to run in Polaris pre-prod):
- Connectivity & cert handshake test (1 hour)
- Short burst soak at target qps for 10 minutes (monitor latency percentiles)
- KV/prefix caching warmup + token-cost measurement run (10 minutes)
- Functional correctness batch (50 prompt pairs)

Logistics: I'll run the smoke-test harness from Redwood's staging account; we will share temporary API keys and a read-only metrics dashboard link. Laura — can you own the RACI for the smoke run with Polaris (drive the ticket and acceptance capture)? Sergio — please surface any known model-variant caveats (quantized vs fp16 path) so we can set the correct default variant for the run.

Thanks — Tessa
From: Diane Nguyen <diane.nguyen@polarisworks.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>, sergio_alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 24 Mar 2028 16:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: PolarisWorks x Redwood — request for solution gate review

Appreciate the checklist and the agenda. Confirmed for Tue 03/28 13:00 PST — invite sent.

Couple quick notes after internal review:
- Our security team confirmed TLS pass-through is fine; they'll provide a short thumbprint verification step during the handshake test.
- Procurement asked if Redwood can provide a short statement of intended reference materials and logos usage — we can follow up after technical signoff.
- For the smoke run, Polaris can supply a test tenancy and will coordinate network ACLs; we expect Redwood to drive the test by providing temporary API keys and a pre-built test harness invocation.

Looking forward to the session.

—
Diane
Head of Integrations | PolarisWorks
